page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.large is a general-purpose virtual instance providing a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hosted on a KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, the instance allocates 4 virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for vector extensions including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI alongside AES cryptography. It is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. The configuration includes no local NVMe storage and no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest computing throughput across standardized tests. Single-core execution registers a Geekbench score of 873.0 and a stress-ng score of 1089.08, situating single-thread execution in lower performance tiers. Multi-threaded processing reaches a Geekbench multi-core score of 2768.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 5201.76. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 32.61 GB/sec, while large-block write bandwidth reaches 28.16 GB/sec. Data manipulation metrics reflect 5.02 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.54 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

Without included local disk storage, persistent data access requires networked storage volumes. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance delivers a balanced hardware profile suitable for routine computing tasks where high-frequency execution or heavy parallel crunching is not mandatory. Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.large is tailored for general-purpose workloads, standard web serving, small-to-medium relational or in-memory caching tiers, microservices, and development environments requiring consistent multi-core access.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.large is a general-purpose virtual machine built on KVM virtualization and x86_64 architecture. The server provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, supported by 35 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction sets. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance includes neither bundled local NVMe storage nor GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage for persistence. Benchmark evaluation reflects entry-level CPU throughput, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 2768.0, 28.16 GB/sec of uncached write memory bandwidth, and 5.02 million Redis SET operations per second. Given its resource footprint and baseline performance, ecs.n2.large is aligned with general-purpose workloads such as light web serving, background processing queues, staging servers, and mid-sized microservices.
